summary: Round 2, measured by mutation in an issued tree on these exact bytes (the staged diff hashes to cf0286e, the same bytes a test-reviewer verdict was already recorded against; this record supersedes that file, so its two minors I did not re-measure are restated below to keep them from vanishing). Round-1 blocking finding M4.47-R1a is FIXED and now pinned: reverting the loop body to `burned.seal(epoch, sealRedriveBudget);` with no `prevEpoch = crossed; prevSeq = landed.sequence(); break;` reddens aCrossedEpochOPENEDBetweenProbeAndSealBecomesTheAncestor with `expected: 3L but was: 1L`, matching the author's red record exactly. Asked specifically whether both halves are pinned: the prevEpoch half IS (dropping `prevEpoch = crossed;` alone reddens the same test, same message); the prevSeq half is NOT, and it is an equivalent mutant rather than a gap -- dropping `prevSeq = landed.sequence();` alone leaves the suite green because the `prevSeq == 0` fallback then re-seals the SAME chain and `CommitLog.seal` adopts the existing Seal, yielding the identical prevSeq at the cost of one recoverChainEnd plus one seal round trip. OpenOnFirstProbeStore is honest: `ChainReplay.firstEntry` is the ONLY stat of a commit-log slot-0 key in the module (grep of `stat(` across sequencer/src/main: the other two are LeaseManager on lease keys, one CheckpointCursor pointer), the walk's probe of epoch 3 is the first and only ABSENT stat of that key, and instrumenting the fixture with the `fired` guard REMOVED still prints exactly one fire -- after the interleave the key exists, so it cannot fire on an unintended path. Not vacuous: neutering the fixture (`fired = true` initially, production untouched) reddens the test with the same `expected: 3L but was: 1L`. Other kills measured on these bytes: `landed.sequence() > 0` -> `>= 0` reddens 4; loop bound `>` -> `>=` reddens theFirstLeaderDoesNotTouchTheReservedUnleasedChain; `burned.seal(crossed, ...)` reddens 4; `predecessor.seal(prevEpoch, ...)` reddens 5; firstInheritableAncestor `atOrigin = false` -> `true` reddens 2 including the new wholly-empty-predecessor test; `replay(..., true)` -> `false` reddens 8. Pristine baseline :sequencer:test green before and after every mutation. I did NOT verify check-mutants: the packet shows it FAILED, my own run in the tree was invalidated because I was mutating sources concurrently, and I killed it rather than report a number I cannot stand behind -- the gate owns that and blocks on its own at pre-commit.

findings.finding: The new arm's boundary is one step away from the assertion. MEASURED: mutating `if (landed.sequence() > 0)` to `if (landed.sequence() > 1)` leaves the whole :sequencer:test suite green. The fixture's interleave writes TWO entries (`stalled.open(1, 2)` then `stalled.commit("seg/stalled", counts(2))`), so the successor's seal redrives to slot 2 and both predicates are true. The minimal real interleave is open-only -- the stalled leader wins slot 0 with its CONTINUE and has not committed yet -- and there the seal lands at slot 1 exactly, which is the only value that separates the two. Same finding as round 1's; re-measured on cf0286e rather than carried over on trust.
findings.failure_scenario: The comparison is edited to `> 1` or `>= 2`, or the seal's slot arithmetic shifts by one, and a crossed epoch that was OPENED in the window but has not committed yet is not recognised as the ancestor. The successor's CONTINUE then names a chain two hops down and skips a genuinely opened one -- the project's own checkLink calls that a broken link -- and the skipped epoch's leader is racing the seal for slot 1, so whether its delta or the seal wins decides whether its offsets are inside what the successor inherits. Nothing goes red.
findings.suggested: A second case whose interleave is `stalled.open(1, 2)` only, asserting prevEpoch == 3 with the seal at slot 1.

findings.finding: The `inherited` half of the origin-meaning change is unconstrained. MEASURED: `r.replayAncestry(prevEpoch, prevSeq, false)` -> `true` -- i.e. reverting `inherited` to the pre-ADR-0037 caveat while leaving `firstInheritableAncestor` fixed -- leaves the entire :sequencer:test suite green. The mirror is well pinned: `replay(..., true)` -> `false` reddens 8 tests. Not an equivalent mutant: with a wholly-empty prevEpoch above a genuine ancestor, `inherited` returns the ancestor's offsets on the staged bytes and an empty map mutated. It is unreachable through the ONLY production caller today -- CommitLog.open <- LocalSequencer.start, where the seal loop guarantees prevEpoch is 0 or a chain with a CONTINUE at slot 0, and a crossed epoch is sealed at slot 0 so it can never be opened afterwards -- which is why this is minor and not major.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller hands CommitLog.open a prevEpoch it did not resolve through firstInheritableAncestor -- M4.6d's rerouting or M5's forwarding, the two the neverOpened javadoc names -- or an existing store carries a pre-fix CONTINUE naming a burned epoch and something reaches it through open() rather than recover(). inherited() answers {} instead of the ancestor's offsets, every stream restarts at 0, and acknowledged offsets are reassigned: the same I2 this commit closes, through the half of the fix the javadoc claims has closed it. Nothing goes red.
findings.suggested: A two-line T1 on ChainReplay.inherited with an empty prevEpoch above a genuine ancestor, asserting the offsets cross rather than come back empty.

findings.finding: Two survivors inside the new loop, both re-measured on cf0286e. (a) Deleting `burned.recoverChainEnd();` leaves the suite green -- observably a request-count difference rather than a different seal, since seal() then proposes at slot 0, loses, adopts or redrives. (b) Dropping `prevSeq = landed.sequence();` while keeping `prevEpoch = crossed; break;` also leaves the suite green, and this one I believe IS equivalent: the `prevSeq == 0 && prevEpoch >= 1` fallback re-seals the chain the loop just chose, sealedAt is already set by recoverChainEnd, and seal() returns the same Seal. Recorded because (a) is a store round trip per crossed epoch on the failover path whose LENGTH is what ADR-0037 had to cost-justify, and no test says whether it must be there.
findings.failure_scenario: recoverChainEnd is added to or removed from the loop and nothing goes red either way, so the per-takeover request count on the crossed run changes silently in the one loop this ADR justifies by a measured distribution.
findings.suggested: Assert a crossed epoch ends with exactly ONE entry after a takeover (no second seal past slot 0), or drop the call and let seal() adjudicate.

findings.finding: CARRIED FORWARD from the test-reviewer verdict recorded at this same hash, because recording overwrites that file and the finding would otherwise vanish. I did NOT re-measure it: the claim is that `closing.continuedAt() > epoch` -> `> Long.MAX_VALUE` (dead LATER-epoch arm) and -> `!= epoch` (the pre-commit form) both leave the suite green, so two of checkLink's three arms are unfalsifiable after the split. What I did check independently is the direction of the loosening from `!=` to `>`: the production mutations that would exploit a wrong `continuedAt` -- `burned.seal(crossed, ...)` and `predecessor.seal(prevEpoch, ...)` -- redden 4 and 5 unit tests respectively, so the seal's continuedAt is not left unguarded by the checker change.
findings.failure_scenario: The LATER-epoch arm is deleted or inverted and nothing notices: the checker stops reporting a chain continuing from an ancestor sealed for an epoch ABOVE it, a fork only the sweep can see. That arm was falsifiable before this commit; the split moved its coverage onto the other half.
findings.suggested: One fixture whose ancestor Seal names a HIGHER epoch than the chain under test.

findings.finding: CARRIED FORWARD from the verdict recorded at this same hash, unverified by me this round: testing.md rule 20's "failing seeds become regression tests" has no in-suite assertion that a FAULTED run has zero violations, so the instrument that FOUND this defect has no red for it. The unit tests do kill the primary mutants (measured above), which is why this stays minor.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change reintroduces the write/read divergence by a route the five hand-built ancestor-seal fixtures do not construct -- all of them put the genuine ancestor at epoch 1 -- and no assertion goes red, so it returns silently as two readers disagreeing about one offset.
findings.suggested: One `assertThat(r.violations()).isEmpty()` inside the ROUGH loop that already runs seeds 0..29, or a named seed-153 ambiguousPut regression test.
